Question: Which Jedi has met the most Sith?
Answer: It has to be Obi-Wan, followed by Ahsoka. He met all the Sith Lords we’ve seen in canon. He dueled and defeated Darth Maul, and then later killed Maul after the latter was no longer a Sith. He met Darth Sidious many times and served him many times. He met Darth Tyrannus, Count Dooku, many times — twice in the Prequel movies and more in other media. He trained and then fought Darth Vader at least twice in the Prequel and Originals, and now in the new TV shows. He not only fought all four Sith shown in canon, but also he had deep, personal connections to all four. A few Jedi who came close as honorable mentions: Anakin(2+1+1): Met Sidious and Tyrannus, both of which he killed. He himself became Vader, and he met Maul briefly. Qui-Gon (2+2): Met Sidious and Maul. Met future Sith in Dooku and Anakin. Ahsoka (2+1): Met Vader, Sidious. Met former Sith Maul, but didn’t meet Tyrannus. Yoda (2+): Met Sidious and Tyrannus. Met Anakin, who’d later be Sith. Didn’t meet Maul. etc.

Question: Do I need to turn off the power to my house when I’m changing a light bulb?
Answer: Why not? Where’s all the negative sentiment in the other answers coming from? Does it cost money to turn off the power? Or does everyone have fragile electrical appliances that would ruin your life whenever you get a power outage? Sure you probably won’t be electrocuted from changing a light bulb, but why take the risk? Does it hurt to turn off the power for a minute? Turning off at least the switch to the light is a basic precaution. Even veteran electricians would do so, and you’re probably not a veteran electrician, so just be safe. If you have a breaker box, even better. Take the extra seconds to flip one switch. Most people pay thousands of dollars every year for insurance. This is free insurance. And this free insurance actually prevents the deadly accident instead of throwing some money on your dead corpse. It literally costs less than going to the bathroom. Just do it.

Question: If it is often claimed that Darth Vader was indeed much more powerful in the Dark Side of the Force than Anakin Skywalker, himself, had been, then does that mean Darth Vader's midichlorian count was actually somewhat higher than Anakin's? If so, how?
Answer: Of course Vader would be more powerful in the dark side of the Force than Anakin. Anakin used the light side of the Force, not the dark. Regarding the Force in general, of course it’s still the case that Vader would be stronger than Anakin. Imagine you have an empty glass. You fill it with water. If you have the same glass, you can still have varying amounts of water. If you filled it halfway, you can keep pouring in more water for there to be more water. You wouldn’t have to get a larger glass to get more water. This is the same for Vader and Anakin. The Force potential is like the empty glass’s potential to be filled with water. You train to fill it up. Vader is stronger than Anakin, because he kept on filling the glass. So he is more connected to the Force and stronger with it. So no, Vader doesn’t have a higher Force potential than Anakin. He simply trained longer and grew up more, to realize more of his potential.

Question: What are your theories on why Obi-Wan is the only one who uses dismemberment as both his fighting style and a last resort?
Answer: I don’t have any theories on why it is, because it is wrong. Dismemberment is neither a fighting style nor a last resort. It’s not special to Obi-Wan either. Dismemberment refers to the act of cutting off someone’s limbs. Yes, it’s an “act”, it’s a single action, not a whole fighting style. Here are just a few examples of dismemberment from individuals not named Obi-Wan: Count Dooku, ended the fight by cutting off Anakin’s arm. Anakin, ended the fight by cutting off Dooku’s hands. Vader, ended the fight by cutting off Luke’s hand. Luke, ended the fight by cutting off Vader’s hand. Do you see a pattern here? Obi-Wan is far from the only one who ends a fight by dismembering the opponent. He is only one among many. And it’s easy to see the utility of dismemberment. After all, an opponent without a hand or a leg would not be able to fight back properly, and you’ve essentially defeated them without having to kill them or inflict more bodily harm.
